vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: taobao
Version: 1.0.3

The skill provides price comparison and coupon retrieval for Chinese e-commerce platforms by querying the maishou88.com API. The script (scripts/main.py) uses a hardcoded affiliate invite code (6110440) and a static OpenID for API requests, which is standard for such utilities and does not pose a security risk to the user or system. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or persistence was found.

llm.summary: This shopping skill is mostly coherent, but it under-discloses fixed tracking/referral identifiers and affiliate-style purchase-link generation.

dimensions.detail: Network access to maishou88.com is purpose-aligned, but the script sends user shopping keywords, product IDs, a fixed OpenID, and an invite code to third-party APIs without adequate user-facing disclosure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses uv plus pip packages aiohttp, argparse, and PyYAML with unpinned versions; this is common but leaves mutable dependency risk, and argparse is unnecessary for Python 3.11 because it is in the standard library.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are straightforward uv commands for search and detail lookup, and maishou88.com is disclosed in the script section, but the broad trigger language and platform-comparison wording do not clearly separate neutral price comparison from third-party aggregator and affiliate-link behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: I found no persistence, background workers, local file reads or writes, privilege escalation, or destructive behavior; the only local sensitive interaction observed is reading the optional MAISHOU_INVITE_CODE environment variable.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Chinese e-commerce price and coupon lookup, and the script does search and detail retrieval; however, it routes all queries through MaiShou APIs and generates share/purchase links using a default invite code without clearly telling users about referral attribution or tracking identifiers.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. It may be useful for Chinese e-commerce search, but assume your product searches and selected item IDs are sent to MaiShou, and generated purchase links may include referral attribution through a built-in invite code unless you override it. Prefer installing only if you are comfortable with that third-party data flow and mutable pip dependency resolution.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Partially supported: shopping search through a third-party aggregator is purpose-aligned and maishou88.com is mentioned, but affiliate/share purchase-link generation and referral identifiers are not clearly disclosed.
[LP3] expected: uv execution and outbound network access fit the skill's purpose, but the artifact does not provide tight permission boundaries or explicit destination scoping beyond documentation.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Supported in part: aggregator-based price lookup is disclosed late in SKILL.md, but the description implies broad platform comparison and the code includes commission fields plus share-link generation with invite attribution.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad shopping trigger is not malicious by itself, but it could invoke the skill for general shopping requests where users may not expect third-party query transmission or referral links.
[AS3] unexpected: Not supported by artifact evidence: the cited text is a homepage URL containing a skills path; I found no code or instruction that enumerates or reads other installed skills.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language UX is consistent with a Chinese-market shopping skill; bilingual disclosure would improve clarity but this is not a material security issue by itself.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Supported as a privacy/transparency concern: user keywords and product selections are sent to MaiShou APIs with a fixed OpenID and optional/default invite code, and this data flow is not fully disclosed.
[SDI-4] expected: The no local file read/write claim is mostly consistent with the reviewed script, though it should be narrowed because the script reads an environment variable and depends on package installation.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Supported: the code embeds a fixed OpenID and default invite code, which can enable correlation or referral attribution unrelated to the user's stated query.
[T09] unexpected: Supported: the AIG finding aligns with the code's fixed OpenID, default invite code, and attributed target URL generation.
[T08] expected: External Python dependencies are expected for the implementation, but unpinned dependencies and the unnecessary argparse package create avoidable supply-chain exposure.
